Chapter Two: The Weight of Obedience and the Loss of Choice
As girls in the FLDS community step into adolescence, the rules that once felt protective start to close in—almost like a cage tightening around them.
That transition from childhood to womanhood isn’t celebrated with joy. Instead, it brings a growing sense of unease. The changes in their bodies come with new expectations. Suddenly, modesty is enforced even more strictly, every interaction with boys is watched, and the pressure to fit in becomes overwhelming.
In this world, personal choice barely exists. Decisions about school, friends, even simple daily routines—they’re all made by someone else. At the center of it all, the community’s leader has more power than ever. His sermons echo warnings—dangers lurking outside, the need for absolute obedience. Even a whisper of doubt isn’t just discouraged; it’s seen as a threat to everyone.
For one teenager, this loss of control hits hardest when marriage is brought up. In the FLDS, marriage isn’t about love or even getting to know someone. It’s a sacred duty, arranged by the prophet. Girls are paired off with men they barely know—sometimes much older, always chosen for reasons that really have nothing to do with what the girl wants.
One day, she’s called in by her father. The talk is short and there’s no back and forth. She’s told: the prophet has chosen a husband for her. This man is little more than a stranger—he’s never shown her real kindness, never tried to understand her. But there’s no space for protest. The choice is made. Her only role is to submit.
The wedding day comes, and it’s nothing like what most people imagine. There’s no joy, no laughter. The bride feels less like a partner and more like an object, her future decided by others. The community gathers to watch, but underneath, there’s a quiet sense of resignation—everyone knows this story. Most have learned to hide their pain behind a mask of faith.
In the days and weeks that follow, reality sets in. She’s now a wife, expected to serve in every way. Her body’s no longer hers, and any sign of resistance is met with anger or cold indifference. The emotional cost is heavy—loneliness, fear, and betrayal become her constant shadows.
Most people outside this world can’t imagine the depth of that loss. It’s not just about freedom—it’s about losing your very sense of self. Her dreams, her desires, even her self-worth are slowly chipped away. Every day, she moves through life numb, doing what’s expected and hoping for rare moments of kindness.
And yet, in the darkest moments, there are sparks of defiance. Maybe it’s a quiet refusal to accept abuse, or just a longing for real connection—a hope that things could be different. These small acts of resistance, though hidden, carry so much power. They’re the first signs of trying to reclaim a self that’s been stolen.
The teachings of the community are meant to stamp out that spirit. But the human soul is resilient. Over time, she starts to question the rules that have always controlled her. Is obedience really the path to salvation, or just a tool for control?
The path to freedom is slow, and it’s painful—full of setbacks and moments of despair. But with every small act of courage, she inches closer to finding her own voice again. It’s not a straight line, and there’s a lot at stake. But that longing for freedom, once it’s sparked, is almost impossible to put out.
